scenes.headline: How Claude turns data into dashboards and films
scenes.sub: Two new templates on the same hosted artifact pages.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Flipbook! Here's what runs underneath Claude's new dashboards and animated explainers.

scenes.text: Neither feature is a new model. Claude writes queries or animation code, and a hosted template runs it.
scenes.say: Neither is a new model. Claude writes queries or animation code, and a hosted template runs it.

scenes.title: A dashboard is a page of queries

steps.say: You connect a warehouse and ask a question in plain words.
Claude writes one database query for every chart.
Each query runs through a connector, on the viewer's own login.
Every chart shows its query and when it last refreshed.
The prompt: the docks on the hill are empty by a quarter past eight, every weekday.
The dashboard answers with stat cards and charts, each one backed by its own query.

scenes.title: How a Motion film gets made
scenes.say: Motion takes the same idea to animation.

items.say: A reviewer pins a comment to a chart, asking Claude for an animation.
Claude writes code that animates text, charts and shapes. No video model.
The template plays that code like a short video.
Someone pins a note to one moment, and Claude changes only that part.
Then you export a video file, or open it in an editor.

steps.say: Claude reports a thirty eight second film, from the map to the empty dock.
The bar has scenes, comments and download. No source mentions a voice.

scenes.title: Two ways to make an explainer

left.title: This site: data in
items: Every digit checked against the article
left.say: On this site, the model writes data, a fixed engine draws it, and every number is checked against the article.

right.title: Motion: code in
items: Edit one number, the rest stays
right.say: Motion lets the model write the animation itself. It can draw anything, and edits stay local.

scenes.text: Code makes a film editable. Only a check against the source keeps its numbers true.
scenes.say: Code makes a film easy to edit. Only a check against the source keeps its numbers true.

recap: Dashboards: queries run on the viewer's login
Motion: model-written code, exported as video
Editable is not the same as checked
scenes.say: Dashboards query as the viewer. Motion is editable code. Editable is not checked.
